description: Ipe is an extremely hard, dense, and durable timber from several Handroanthus species (formerly placed in Tabebuia), mainly H. serratifolius and H. impetiginosus. It is best known for outdoor decking, boardwalks, and docks, and is also used for flooring and turning. Its hardness and fine dust make it hard on tools and dusty to machine.

hazards.summary: A worker developed occupational asthma from ipe dust, confirmed when a controlled bronchial challenge with the dust triggered a delayed asthma attack. A separate report describes asthma from bethabara, a trade name for ipe.
A construction worker developed recurring patches of skin inflammation and darkening linked to handling ipe. Ipe contains naphthoquinones, a class of compounds known to sensitize skin.
All wood dust, including ipe, is classified by IARC as carcinogenic to humans, mainly linked to cancers of the nose and sinuses after long-term exposure.

related_species_note: Ipe is sold under many names and from several Handroanthus species; the asthma evidence comes from wood identified only as ipe or bethabara (Tabebuia spp.), so assume any species sold as ipe can act the same way.
image_prompt: Photorealistic studio photograph of a freshly planed ipe (Handroanthus spp.) board, shot at a low three-quarter angle so the face grain fills most of the frame. Dense olive-brown to deep reddish-brown heartwood with subtle darker and lighter striping, and a narrow band of pale yellowish-white sapwood along one edge. Fine, tight texture with interlocked grain giving a faint ribbon stripe, tiny pores sometimes flecked with yellowish powdery deposits, moderate natural luster. Soft diffused daylight from upper left, gentle falloff, neutral warm-grey seamless background, shallow depth of field with the near edge tack-sharp. No text, no logos, no hands, no tools, no finish or varnish, natural unfinished wood. Wide 1200x630 composition (1.91:1) with the board centered and margin on both sides for cropping.
image_alt: Planed board of ipe with dense olive-brown to reddish-brown heartwood, faint ribbon striping, and a thin edge of pale sapwood.
notes_internal: Botanical names checked only against GBIF backbone (POWO/WFO blocked: 403/TLS errors) - set unverified. Most-traded species (H. serratifolius, H. impetiginosus) taken from a search summary of CITES CoP18 Doc.105.3 that could not be opened (403); verify. Algranti-2005: patch tests and specific IgE were NEGATIVE; only SIC and skin prick positive. Skin hazard is level 3: Landry-2018 has no abstract (testing unknown; may be level 1 if patch-tested). Lapachol lead not sourced: no primary linking lapachol in ipe wood to dermatitis was found on PubMed (Estlander 2001 PMID 11260236 reports lapachol patch reactions but not tied to ipe). Cordero 1951 (PMID 14844035, 'Occupational sensitization to Tecoma avellanedae sawdust') not cited: no abstract, route unknown. 'Brazilian walnut' alias collides with imbuia; kept here as decking trade name - review. No reports for a given effect does not mean the wood is safe.
